questions.text: Why does a context budget reserve space for generation before allocating input components?

options.A: To ensure the response has room within the model’s total token limit.
options.B: To guarantee that every retrieved document is factually accurate.
options.C: To prevent conversation history from influencing the response.
options.D: To convert unused input tokens into permanent model knowledge.

questions.explanation: Input components and generated output consume the available context capacity; reserving output space avoids filling it entirely with input.

questions.text: A coding assistant includes 50 tool definitions, mostly unrelated retrieved documents, and a long conversation history in every request. Which change best follows dynamic context assembly?

options.A: Always fill the entire context window with additional historical messages.
options.B: Remove the current query whenever the context exceeds its budget.
options.C: Select tools and documents for the current task and compress older history.
options.D: Include all tools unchanged and reduce only the response budget.

questions.explanation: Dynamic assembly prioritizes task-relevant tools, evidence, and history while preserving output room.

questions.text: The history compressor totals only self.turns, moves old pairs into self.summaries, and stops when len(self.turns) <= 4. get_context() includes both lists. What limitation follows?

options.A: It deletes all summaries before returning the final context.
options.B: It guarantees the assembled history always fits max_history_tokens.
options.C: It measures summary tokens but never measures recent turn tokens.
options.D: Returned context can exceed the limit because summaries are uncounted and four turns may remain oversized.

questions.explanation: The loop’s budget excludes summaries, and its four-turn floor can retain oversized recent content. The full returned context is not guaranteed to fit the configured history limit.
